commitResults.messageTitle: Add file storage for task list persistence
commitResults.messageBody:
Save tasks to './data/oz.txt' automatically whenever the task list
is modified (on adding, marking, unmarking, or deleting tasks).

Load existing tasks from the storage file on chatbot startup, with
graceful handling for missing files and malformed task records.

Update .gitignore to exclude runtime storage data.

commitResults.messageTitle: Support date and time parsing for tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Parse deadline and event dates into java.time objects using
TaskDateTime, supporting formats such as yyyy-MM-dd and d/M/yyyy HHmm.

Display dates formatted as 'MMM dd yyyy' and 'MMM dd yyyy, h:mma'
while persisting standard representations to disk.

commitResults.messageTitle: Support time for events and add input validation
commitResults.messageBody:
Allow events and deadlines to accept time components in addition to
dates in TaskDateTime, supporting formats such as 1800 and 6pm.

Validate that an event's start date/time is not after its end date/time
in Event and ensure task descriptions and date arguments are non-empty
in Oz.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add 'on' command to filter tasks by date
commitResults.messageBody:
Implement the 'on <date>' command to find and list all deadlines and
events occurring on a specific date.

Add occursOn method to Task, Deadlines, and Event to check date
matching and interval overlap.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Storage class for task persistence
commitResults.messageBody:
Extract file reading, writing, and parsing logic from Oz into a
dedicated Storage class.

Oz now instantiates Storage with the storage file path and delegates
task loading and saving operations to it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract TaskList class to manage tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Encapsulate task list collection and mutation operations in a
dedicated TaskList class.

Update Storage and Oz to use TaskList rather than interacting directly
with raw ArrayList collections.

commitResults.messageTitle: Organize classes into packages under src/main/java
commitResults.messageBody:
Move classes into dedicated packages under src/main/java/oz/ to
improve modularity and maintainability.

Group classes into oz, oz.exception, oz.storage, and oz.task packages,
updating package declarations and imports accordingly.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests for TaskDateTime and TaskList
commitResults.messageBody:
Add JUnit 5 test classes TaskDateTimeTest and TaskListTest under
src/test/java/oz/task/ following Gradle conventions.

Cover valid date/time parsing variations, error handling for invalid
or empty inputs, date comparisons, and task list mutations.

commitResults.messageTitle: Expand JUnit test suites and document 50% coverage
commitResults.messageBody:
Add comprehensive test suites for Event and Deadlines, and extend
test cases for TaskDateTime and TaskList to target top-value methods.

Update AGENTS.md to document the 50% test coverage requirement.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add comprehensive Javadoc comments across codebase
commitResults.messageBody:
Add Javadoc header comments to all classes, constructors, methods,
and fields across the project.

Verify full Javadoc generation via Gradle with zero warnings.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add seedu-java-coding-standard skill and refactor code
commitResults.messageBody:
Create seedu-java-coding-standard skill in .agents/skills/ based on
SE-EDU Java Coding Standard (Basic + Intermediate) guidelines.

Mandate coding standard in AGENTS.md and refactor variable names
and argument patterns to eliminate abbreviations and single letters.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add seedu-git-standard skill and update AGENTS.md
commitResults.messageBody:
The repository lacks a dedicated project skill for SE-EDU Git
conventions, and AGENTS.md does not mandate commit message structure.

Inconsistent commit formatting makes it difficult for reviewers to
quickly understand the rationale behind changes.

Let's create the seedu-git-standard skill under .agents/skills/ and
update AGENTS.md to mandate adherence to SE-EDU Git conventions.

Defining a dedicated skill and linking it in AGENTS.md ensures all
future commits consistently follow structured commit message standards.

Refer to SE-EDU Git conventions:
https://se-education.org/guides/conventions/git.html

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find command to search tasks by keyword
commitResults.messageBody:
Users can view, add, and query tasks by date, but cannot search
tasks matching a specific keyword.

Manually scanning the entire task list to locate specific tasks is
cumbersome when the list grows large.

Let's introduce a find command to search and list all tasks whose
descriptions match a given keyword case-insensitively.

Adding containsKeyword to Task and findTasksByKeyword to TaskList
encapsulates search logic in the task domain layer.

Unit tests in TaskListTest cover matching, non-matching, and
case-insensitive search scenarios.

commitResults.messageTitle: Set up Checkstyle and fix code style violations
commitResults.messageBody:
The project lacks automated static code analysis, making it easy for
style and formatting inconsistencies to slip into the codebase.

Manual code reviews are error-prone and time-consuming when checking
style rules such as indentation, import order, and declaration ordering.

Let's integrate Checkstyle 14.1.0 into build.gradle using the rules
from AddressBook Level 3, and resolve all style violations across the
source files.

Automating style checking via Gradle tasks (checkstyleMain,
checkstyleTest) enforces continuous compliance with the SE-EDU Java
Coding Standard during builds.

Refer to SE-EDU Checkstyle tutorial:
https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/checkstyle.html

commitResults.messageTitle: Add basic GUI and resources for future GUI development
Add JavaFX GUI and connect to chatbot logic
commitResults.messageBody:
Oz operates exclusively as a command-line interface chatbot where
command parsing, task operations, and terminal I/O are tightly coupled
within the main loop.
A graphical user interface provides a more intuitive, responsive, and
visually engaging user experience. However, adding the GUI should not
duplicate domain logic or break console interactions.
Let's introduce a JavaFX GUI consisting of Main, DialogBox, and
Launcher, while moving resource assets into src/main/resources/.
Refactor Oz to extract a public getResponse(String) method that both
the CLI and GUI invoke to process commands. In addition, add unit tests
for DialogBox and the response engine.
Extracting getResponse(String) preserves a single source of truth for
command parsing and task state manipulation. CLI run() continues to
handle terminal streams and dividers without regressions, while the GUI
renders clean chat bubbles via DialogBox with speech-flipped avatars.

commitResults.messageTitle: Migrate JavaFX GUI to FXML with styling and tests
commitResults.messageBody:
The GUI layout and dialog components are constructed programmatically
in Java code, mixing view presentation with controller logic. Window
closure on exit commands is not handled gracefully.
Constructing UI components imperatively in Java makes layout changes
tedious, clutters controller logic, and prevents clean styling via CSS.
Furthermore, the GUI should smoothly close the window when an exit
command is issued without abruptly terminating mid-conversation.
Let's migrate the UI to declarative FXML layouts (MainWindow.fxml and
DialogBox.fxml) paired with custom CSS stylesheets (main.css and
dialog-box.css). Refactor DialogBox as a custom FXML root component,
connect MainWindow as the controller, and introduce an exit transition
on the bye command using PauseTransition. Additionally, add a GUI unit
test suite covering DialogBox, MainWindow, and Oz responses.
Separating markup into FXML and visual styling into CSS adheres to the
MVC pattern and eases future interface adjustments. Handling exit via
isExit() and PauseTransition ensures the user sees the farewell dialog
bubble before the window closes, preserving a pleasant UX.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tag command responses for dynamic dialog styling
commitResults.messageBody:
All chatbot responses returned by Oz are plain strings, and the GUI
renders every reply in a dialog bubble with identical styling.

Users cannot visually distinguish between different types of actions
(such as adding tasks, updating completion status, or deleting tasks),
reducing the visual feedback and responsiveness of the chat interface.

Let's update getResponse in Oz to return a Pair<String, String>
containing the response message and a command tag (such as AddCommand,
ChangeMarkCommand, and DeleteCommand). In MainWindow, forward this tag
to DialogBox.getOzDialog, which applies custom CSS classes (add-label,
marked-label, delete-label) to colorize dialog bubbles. Update
stylesheets with background assets and styling, and expand unit tests
to verify command tagging and styling behavior.

Returning a pair passes command metadata to the GUI while keeping the
CLI command loop fully functional. Applying CSS classes dynamically in
DialogBox decouples visual appearance from controller logic and keeps
the presentation declarative.

commitResults.messageTitle: Resolve code review feedback on task components
commitResults.messageBody:
Review comments from peer reviews highlight naming inconsistencies in
task domain classes, ambiguous method names, prepositional field names,
and minor Checkstyle layout discrepancies. Specifically, Deadlines uses
a plural noun unlike ToDo and Event, Storage#parseTaskFromFile parses a
single line rather than an entire file, Event fields use prepositions
from and to, and Task mark/unmark methods are ambiguous at call sites.

Inconsistent naming increases cognitive overhead for maintainers and
violates the SE-EDU Java Coding Standard conventions. Ambiguous method
names obscure the exact state change being performed, and plural class
names for single task instances miscommunicate their cardinality.

Let's resolve all review feedback by:
- Renaming Deadlines to Deadline and updating all references and tests.
- Renaming parseTaskFromFile to parseTaskLine in Storage.
- Renaming Event fields from and to to startDateTime and endDateTime.
- Renaming Task mark/unmark methods to markAsDone/markAsNotDone.
- Adding missing field Javadocs and wrapping long lines to enforce the
  110-character line length standard.

Singular naming for task classes standardizes domain vocabulary. Using
markAsDone and markAsNotDone clarifies intent directly at the call
site without having to inspect method documentation. Wrapping long
expressions and documenting all fields to keep with style guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add assertions to ensure invariants hold
commitResults.messageBody:
Task code dereferences descriptions, date-times, and task-list entries
assuming they are non-null and internally consistent.

A programming error that breaks an invariant could otherwise surface later
as a less useful NullPointerException.

Let's

* Add assertions at construction, collection, storage, and command
boundaries, then add focused tests for assertion failures.

* Use assertions only for internal assumptions. User input and malformed
storage remain validated with OzException because assertions may be
disabled at runtime.

The GUI classes and response tests violate the repository's style
checks for import grouping and switch indentation. These differences
make the code inconsistent and prevent Checkstyle from passing.

Align the affected imports and switch branches with the configured
standard. Keep this formatting change separate from behavior
refactoring so its scope is easy to review.

Validation: all 46 JUnit tests and both Checkstyle tasks pass on Java 25.

The response method mixes command dispatch, argument validation,
task operations, persistence, and formatting in one long conditional.
This makes individual commands difficult to understand and maintain.

Extract a named handler for each command and keep input parsing and
error reporting in getResponse. Use a small dispatch switch with an
explicit unknown-command branch to expose the supported operations.

Keep command behavior unchanged and add regression tests for invalid
arguments, task-number boundaries, and date-filtered results. This
applies the course guidelines on short methods and abstraction levels.

Validation: all 49 JUnit tests and both Checkstyle tasks pass on Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Share task addition and list formatting
commitResults.messageBody:
The three add handlers repeat task insertion, saving, and confirmation.
The three listing handlers also repeat the same numbering loop. Each
copy can drift when persistence or response formatting changes.

Extract shared helpers for adding a validated task and formatting a
numbered list. Keep validation, headings, and empty-result messages in
the individual handlers because those rules belong to each command.

Add regression tests for persisted additions, task counts, keyword
result numbering, and whitespace. This follows the course guideline
to minimize duplication without introducing unnecessary abstractions.

Validation: all 51 JUnit tests and both Checkstyle tasks pass on Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Separate storage parsing by task type
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage parsing combines common header validation, completion status,
and three task-specific formats in one long method. This obscures the
validation rules for each stored task type.

Extract focused parsers for todos, deadlines, and events, and route
them through a short switch with an explicit unknown-type error.
Keep status restoration in the common parser so each responsibility
can be read independently without changing the storage format.

Add persistence tests for all task types and completion states,
corrupted records, missing files, blank lines, byte-order marks, and
literal pipes in todo descriptions. This applies the course guidelines
on short methods and a single level of abstraction.

Validation: all 56 JUnit tests and both Checkstyle tasks pass on Java 25.

The storage parser uses numeric field positions and counts alongside
literal type and completion codes. Their meaning is implicit, and the
reader and writers independently repeat the same storage codes.

Name field positions, field counts, the separator, and the byte-order
mark in Storage. Define completion codes on Task and type codes on
each task subtype, where serialization already belongs, and reuse them
when loading and displaying tasks.

Keep the file format unchanged. Strengthen the round-trip test with
literal expected file contents so matching reader and writer changes
cannot silently change the persistence contract.

Validation: all 56 tests and both Checkstyle tasks pass on Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name application defaults and display formats
commitResults.messageBody:
Application defaults and display patterns appear as inline literals.
The storage path and date display pattern are also repeated, allowing
the console, GUI, and task descriptions to diverge when edited.

Name the default storage path and farewell display duration. Share
the date formatter between task descriptions and filtered headings,
and name the hour-only and minute-inclusive time formatters.

Keep the constants with their owning classes to make their purpose
clear without adding a general-purpose constants container. Preserve
existing behavior and add clock-format boundary coverage.

Validation: all 57 tests and both Checkstyle tasks pass on Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Flatten date display with a guard clause
commitResults.messageBody:
Date display nests the choice of time format inside a hasTime branch.
The date-only path appears after the more involved time-format logic.

Return the date-only result immediately when no time is present.
Keep time formatting at the main indentation level so its two formats
can be read without tracking an enclosing conditional.

Apply Replace Nested Conditional with Guard Clauses and preserve all
output. Add a regression test distinguishing a date-only value from
an explicitly entered midnight.

Validation: all 58 tests and both Checkstyle tasks pass on Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace date constructor flag with factories
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskDateTime construction takes a boolean whose meaning is hidden at
the call site. Callers must also convert date-only values to midnight
before passing false, coupling them to the internal representation.

Expose fromDate and fromDateTime factories and make the flag-based
constructor private. Update parsing to call the explicit factories.
Keep the flag internally because display and storage must distinguish
a date-only value from an explicitly supplied midnight.

Apply Replace Parameter with Explicit Methods. Test both factories
for display, storage, and chronological comparison behavior.

Validation: all 60 tests and both Checkstyle tasks pass on Java 25.
Add assertions to ensure invariants hold

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix date invariant tests broken by merge conflict
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskInvariantTest invokes the flag-based TaskDateTime constructor
directly to verify constructor assertions.

Resolving the merge conflict between branch-A-Assertions and
branch-A-CodeQuality brought in tests targeting the old public
constructor after it was made private in favor of explicit factory
methods. This causes compilation errors in the test suite.

Let's

* Guard TaskDateTime.fromDate and TaskDateTime.fromDateTime with
  assertions against null inputs.
* Update TaskInvariantTest to instantiate dates via fromDateTime.
* Replace the direct private-constructor test with assertions on the
  public factory methods.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor task filter to use streams
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskList uses loop through tasks to build filtered lists

The loop logic obscures the filter logic and repeats code structure.

Let's
- Replace both filter loops with stream filters and collect the results
  into a new list
- Collect into ArrayList to preserve existing method contracts and task
  ordering

Oz supports only one-off tasks.

Users need weekly series with independently tracked occurrences.

Add recurring-event commands, persistence, tests, and documentation.

Keep recurrence weekly and same-day to limit the feature's scope.

Use a separate task type to preserve existing event behavior.

Recurring records use the R type and a reserved zero status field.

Resource paths, style names, and validation messages are embedded
directly at their usage sites.

These literals are difficult to identify and maintain consistently as
the application grows.

Let's extract the literals into named constants owned by their relevant
classes.

Keep the constants local to avoid unnecessary coupling while preserving
all existing values and behavior.

Recurring event commands repeat the same date in both event time
arguments.

This redundancy makes recurring syntax easy to confuse with ordinary
event syntax.

Let's accept the date once through /on and parse /start and /end as time-only
values. Update the related tests and documentation.

Keep /from and /to exclusive to ordinary events so each prefix retains
a consistent input format.

Both participants use large avatars in the narrow chat window.

The images consume space that is more useful for task information.

Remove the user avatar and reduce the Oz avatar to 40 pixels.

Keep a small Oz image to distinguish app replies while presenting user
commands as compact, right-aligned bubbles.

Update dialog tests to cover the new asymmetric structure.

The window can resize, but fixed dialog sizing does not adapt well.

Long replies can lose useful width or resist wrapping in narrow windows.

Set practical stage limits and bind bubbles to the available row width.

Retain the compact launch size while allowing wider windows to show more
message content and narrower windows to wrap it safely.

Add layout tests for the new minimum dimensions.

Blank input creates an empty user bubble and an unnecessary reply.

That interaction adds clutter without performing a useful command.

Disable Send for blank text and guard the input handler as a fallback.

Use a whitespace-aware binding so spaces alone do not enable submission,
and release the binding safely when the application exits.

Add a GUI test for blank and non-blank button states.

The GUI opens without guidance and long replies are difficult to reuse.

Users must already know the command syntax and repeatedly restore focus.

Show example commands, clarify the prompt, maintain keyboard focus, and
add a context-menu action for copying any message.

Keep the guidance concise so it helps first-time users without consuming
much conversation space.

Add GUI tests for the prompt, welcome message, and copy action.

commitResults.messageTitle: Improve GUI message interaction and control styles
commitResults.messageBody:
Dialog messages use non-selectable labels and disabled send buttons fade
into the window background.

Users cannot select partial message text, and the default 40% opacity on
inactive buttons creates an indistinct, washed-out appearance.

Let's replace message labels with uneditable TextAreas and style disabled
buttons with solid grey and full opacity.

TextAreas allow native cursor text selection without nested scrollbars,
while solid grey disabled styling provides clear feedback without
relying on translucency.

Update DialogBoxTest and MainWindowTest to assert TextArea properties.

commitResults.messageTitle: Adopt Professor Pig persona for command responses
commitResults.messageBody:
The chatbot responses use generic phrasing that does not reflect the
visual character theme of the avatar.

The avatar represents a Professor Pig, but the textual
feedback lacks thematic personality and immersion.

Let's:
* Update greeting, farewell, task modification, and query messages to
  use concise porcine mannerisms and inventor motifs.
* Revise error prefixes and unknown command feedback to reflect the
  persona's scientific exasperation.
* Update the GUI welcome message and synchronize existing unit test
  assertions with the revised responses.
* Fix Checkstyle import ordering in MainWindowTest.

Short, punchy responses are used to prevent dialog clutter in the GUI
while still establishing a clear, unique personality.

commitResults.messageTitle: Forbid storage delimiter in task creation input
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks are saved to disk using a vertical pipe delimiter.

When a user includes the '|' character in task creation commands,
the serialized record structure becomes ambiguous and causes line
corruption when reloading tasks from storage.

Let's validate all task creation input across todo, deadline,
event, and recurring commands to reject any input containing '|',
and return a clear error explaining that the character is reserved.

Validating before command execution protects disk persistence from
becoming corrupt while providing immediate feedback to the user.

Credit to user Gnanes99 (https://github.com/Gnanes99) for the insight
to forbid the storage delimiter.
Add unit tests verifying rejection of '|' across all task types.

commitResults.messageTitle: Detect duplicate and misplaced command flags
commitResults.messageBody:
Commands use regular expressions that do not explicitly validate flag
occurrences or ordering.

Users can supply duplicate parameter flags like /by or /from, place
/to before /from in event commands, or pass flags to commands that do
not accept them, leading to confusing error messages or swallowed
parameters.

Let's:
* Count parameter flags across task commands to detect duplicate flags.
* Verify flag order so /from must precede /to in event commands and
  recurring parameters appear in valid sequence.
* Forbid unexpected flags in todo, deadline, event, mark, and unmark.
* Enforce that the bye command takes no trailing arguments.

Explicit pre-validation gives clear, actionable diagnostic messages
explaining exactly which parameter is duplicated, misplaced, or
unexpected rather than relying on generic regex mismatches.

Add unit tests covering duplicate, misplaced, and unexpected flags.

commitResults.messageTitle: Provide descriptive index validation error messages
commitResults.messageBody:
Task index parsing uses generic error messages that do not clarify the
exact reason an index argument is invalid.

Users receiving errors for empty lists, non-numeric inputs, negative
numbers, or out-of-range task numbers receive generic messages that do
not explain the allowable range or empty state.

Let's:
* Distinguish empty arguments, non-numeric strings, and non-positive
  numbers with dedicated messages.
* Inform the user when referencing tasks while the task list is empty.
* Provide the valid 1-based index range when a supplied number exceeds
  the current list size.

Structured index validation guides users directly to the proper command
syntax and bounds without ambiguity.

Add unit tests verifying all descriptive index failure branches.

commitResults.messageTitle: Enforce strict date resolution for task dates
commitResults.messageBody:
Task date and time parsing uses lenient date resolution patterns.

Under lenient resolution, invalid calendar dates like February 30 or
April 31 are silently adjusted to valid dates (e.g., February 28),
storing dates different from what the user entered.

Let's:
* Update input and storage date formatters to use ResolverStyle.STRICT
  with proleptic-year patterns ('uuuu').
* Configure minute and second defaults to retain flexible time inputs.
* Detect DateTimeParseException instances caused by invalid dates and
  return a dedicated error message for impossible calendar days.

Strict date resolution guarantees that all persisted and displayed
dates exist on the calendar without silent data alteration.

Add unit tests verifying rejection of February 30, April 31, and
non-leap year February 29 dates.

commitResults.messageTitle: Disallow redundant mark and unmark operations
commitResults.messageBody:
Mark and unmark operations silently reapply the completion status
when a task is already in the target state.

Users receive a success response implying that the state was updated,
even though the task was already completed or incomplete.

Let's:
* Add isDone getter method to the Task class.
* Check task completion status before executing mark and unmark.
* Throw an OzException when attempting to mark an already completed
  task or unmark an incomplete task.

Providing explicit feedback for redundant state changes alerts users
to duplicate commands and clarifies the actual ledger status.

Add unit tests verifying error responses for redundant mark and unmark
commands.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle file write permission and storage save errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage save failures are caught internally and printed to standard
output without notifying the user or rolling back in-memory state.

When file access is denied or a file is read-only, GUI users receive no
feedback that persistence failed, leaving the in-memory task list out
of sync with the disk.

Let's:
* Check file writability and throw an OzException on access denial.
* Propagate storage save exceptions to command handlers and GUI
  responses.
* Add indexed insertion to TaskList to allow in-memory rollbacks.
* Roll back task additions, deletions, and status toggles if saving
  fails.

Propagating write errors surfaces permission issues directly to the
user, while rollback prevents memory and disk data inconsistency.

Add unit tests for read-only save rejection and state rollback.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add automated unit tests for non-GUI components
commitResults.messageBody:
Automated unit tests cover primary happy paths but omit dedicated
tests for ToDo, base Task methods, CLI loop execution, and key
defensive rollback paths.

Without comprehensive automated testing across core non-GUI logic,
edge cases in parsing, corrupted storage recovery, and persistence
failure rollbacks remain susceptible to regressions.

Let's:
* Add ToDoTest and TaskTest for task formatting, search, and state.
* Add CommandTypeTest and OzExceptionTest for enums and exceptions.
* Add OzRunTest to verify CLI command execution via I/O redirection.
* Expand TaskListTest for indexed insertion and null safety.
* Expand TaskDateTimeTest for date and time parsing boundary checks.
* Expand StorageTest for corrupted recurring records and save overloads.
* Expand OzResponseTest for flag validation and state rollbacks.

Covering non-GUI logic thoroughly achieves high confidence and over 90%
code coverage without introducing brittle headless JavaFX tests.

Oz contains message constants over the line-length limit and a line with trailing whitespace.

These violations prevent Checkstyle from providing a green refactoring baseline.

Wrap the long constants and remove the trailing whitespace.

Keep every string value unchanged so the cleanup cannot alter command behavior.

All tests and both Checkstyle targets pass.

Oz returns JavaFX Pair values from its public response API.

This couples command logic to a GUI utility and hides result meaning.

Introduce CommandResult and update callers to use message and type.

Use a record to keep result data immutable and accessors explicit.

All tests and both Checkstyle targets pass.

CommandType labels response categories such as ERROR, BLANK, and DEFAULT.

The name becomes ambiguous before introducing executable command types.

Rename the enum and update response, UI, and test references.

Use ResponseType to distinguish presentation metadata from commands.

All tests and both Checkstyle targets pass.

Oz owns both command processing and the interactive console loop.

Mixing UI input and output with application logic obscures its role.

Move scanning, banners, and printing into a dedicated ConsoleUi.

Keep Oz.main stable and route console commands through getResponse.

Console regression tests, all tests, and Checkstyle pass.

Oz tokenizes raw input before routing every command.

Keeping parsing in the controller mixes abstraction levels and hinders tests.

Move command tokenization into CommandParser and return ParsedCommand.

Use a record so parsed parts are immutable and named explicitly.

Parser tests, all tests, and both Checkstyle targets pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract task creation parsing from Oz
commitResults.messageBody:
Oz validates and constructs every task type inside command handlers.

This mixes low-level grammar rules with task persistence and responses.

Move task argument parsing and validation into TaskParser.

Keep persistence in Oz so parsing remains stateless and independently testable.

Focused parser tests, all tests, and Checkstyle pass.

Oz owns task state, persistence calls, and rollback for every mutation.

This duplicates a critical consistency rule across several command handlers.

Move task queries and persisted mutations into TaskService.

Keep rollback beside each mutation so failed saves restore memory first.

Service tests, all tests, and both Checkstyle targets pass.

Oz parses task indexes, mutation flags, and recurring dates inline.

This mixes input validation with command execution and response formatting.

Move task-target parsing into TaskTargetParser and TaskTarget.

Keep command-specific parsing entry points so each caller states its intent.

Parser tests, all tests, and both Checkstyle targets pass.

Oz builds list, mutation, and recurring-occurrence messages inline.

This mixes presentation details into otherwise concise command handlers.

Move task message construction into TaskResponseFormatter.

Remove an occurrence helper made redundant by the formatter boundary.

Formatter tests, all tests, and both Checkstyle targets pass.

Storage interprets every task record while also handling file input.

This mixes domain parsing details with file-system orchestration.

Move persisted record conversion into TaskRecordParser.

Keep the parser package-private because the format is a storage detail.

Parser tests, all tests, and both Checkstyle targets pass.

Storage exposes overloads for both ArrayList and the domain TaskList.

This couples file persistence to collection implementations and domain state.

Accept List<Task> and pass TaskList contents from TaskService.

Use the interface type to keep the storage boundary small and reusable.

All tests and both Checkstyle targets pass on Java 25.

Storage load and save methods mix workflows with low-level mechanics.

This obscures their happy paths and makes failures harder to locate.

Extract record normalization, reporting, setup, and serialization helpers.

Keep each public method at one abstraction level with explicit errors.

All tests and both Checkstyle targets pass on Java 25.

Task parsers duplicate flag matching and delimiter validation logic.

This risks inconsistent boundaries and repeated error handling.

Move shared argument checks into CommandArgumentValidator.

Keep it package-private because validation is an internal parser detail.

Validator tests, all tests, and both Checkstyle targets pass.

TaskParser owns recurring flags, fields, intervals, and date assembly.

This gives one parser multiple detailed grammars and abstraction levels.

Move recurring command parsing into RecurringEventParser.

Preserve TaskParser as the stable public entry point for callers.

Recurring parser tests, all tests, and Checkstyle targets pass.

TaskDateTime owns input grammars, retry logic, and value behavior.

This combines parsing mechanics with formatting and comparisons.

Move supported input parsing into TaskDateTimeParser.

Keep TaskDateTime as the stable public facade and domain value.

Parser tests, all tests, and both Checkstyle targets pass.

Callers depend directly on TaskDateTime's display formatter constant.

This exposes formatting mechanics and permits locale-sensitive output.

Add a date-formatting method and use an explicit English locale.

Keep presentation rules centralized behind the TaskDateTime API.

All tests and both Checkstyle targets pass on Java 25.

TaskList retains constructor lists and exposes its mutable collection.

Callers can therefore alter task membership without domain operations.

Copy incoming lists and return immutable List snapshots.

Depend on the List interface to hide the internal implementation.

Encapsulation tests, all tests, and Checkstyle targets pass.

RecurringEvent owns schedule validation, calculation, and event state.

This combines the recurrence rule with occurrence completion behavior.

Move weekly schedule behavior into WeeklyRecurrence.

Keep the rule package-private as part of the task-domain model.

Rule tests, all tests, and both Checkstyle targets pass.

Task descriptions remain mutable after construction.

Default-locale case conversion can make searches inconsistent.

Make descriptions final and keep completion state private.

Normalize keyword searches using the locale-neutral root locale.

All tests and both Checkstyle targets pass on Java 25.

DialogBox construction mixes FXML loading with control setup.

A load failure prints a trace and leaves the control unusable.

Extract focused setup methods and isolate clipboard behavior.

Fail fast so callers never receive a partially initialized dialog.

All tests and both Checkstyle targets pass on Java 25.

MainWindow mixes conversation rendering with shutdown mechanics.

This obscures the normal command flow and makes it harder to test.

Extract display and delayed-exit operations into focused methods.

Use a guard clause so the normal refocus path remains prominent.

GUI regression tests and both Checkstyle targets pass on Java 25.

Task creation methods mix flag policy with object construction.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document project setup and add GUI run task
commitResults.messageBody:
The project README contains outdated template instructions, while Gradle
only provides a task for launching the command-line interface.

Users need accurate setup, command, build, attribution, and execution
instructions for the completed Oz application.

Let's replace the template README with project-specific documentation and
add a runGui task that launches the JavaFX entry point.

Keep the existing run task for the command-line interface so established
development workflows remain unchanged.

Document the supported date formats, JAR packaging, JaCoCo usage,
third-party software, and use of AI assistance.

The packaged JAR uses Oz as its main class and starts the CLI.

This prevents users from opening the JavaFX interface through the JAR.

Let's set Launcher as the application main class so packaged builds start the GUI.

Use the dedicated launcher to initialize JavaFX without classpath issues.

The runGui task continues to use the same launcher.

The user guide mixes developer instructions with command documentation.
Some reused ideas and image assets also need clearer attribution.

Users need concise guidance for every supported Oz command. Reused work
must also remain clearly credited.

Let's restructure the guide around features and examples, add the
missing
credits, and remove the redundant manual test plan.

The focused layout improves usability while retaining important command
details. Task behavior and automated tests remain unchanged.

Dialog bubbles estimate their height using a separate Text node. Its
dimensions can differ from the TextArea viewport, causing long messages
to be clipped.

Measure the TextArea content after its viewport is laid out and include
the surrounding control decoration in the calculated height.

This uses the dimensions of the displayed content and adds a regression
test for long task lists.

GeraldFSE identified the clipping during smoke testing:
https://github.com/NUS-CS2103-AY2627-S1/forum/issues/522#issuecomment-5752656706
